betterCitation: Jorge Luis Borges, Funes, the Memorious, in Ficciones, closing pages (trans. Anthony Kerrigan, 1962)
reason: REFUTED ON THE NOTE, NOT ON THE CITATION. The source line is right and I can prove it harder than the verifier did, but the note that would ship with it states a falsehood about a named translation, which is the one thing this track forbids above all others. Take the citation first. I fetched the same scan, extracted and inflated its content streams and read the whole story in place. It is the Grove Ficciones: the running heads alternate Jorge Luis Borges and Ficciones, the story heading is FUNES, THE MEMORIOUS with the comma, the Artifices prologue above it is dated Buenos Aires August 29, 1944, the story closes with the date 1942, and the last line of the story, which the verifier's evidence never mentions, is an explicit credit: Translated by ANTHONY KERRIGAN. That credit line settles the translator by itself. The passage reads: Without effort, he had learned English, French, Portuguese, Latin. I suspect, nevertheless, that he was not very capable of thought. To think is to forget a difference, to generalize, to abstract. In the overly replete world of Funes there were nothing but details, almost contiguous details. So the shipped quotation is Kerrigan's verbatim, to the character, and the locator holds: it is the third paragraph from the end of the story. Now the break. The note says: The wording proposed matches the later Hurley translation. I read the proposal in proposals-fiction-essay.json. The proposed quotation was To think is to forget differences, generalize, make abstractions, with translator James E. Irby, 1962, and the work given as Labyrinths, New Directions, 1962. That is Irby's wording, not Hurley's. Irby's Labyrinths reads To think is to forget differences, generalize, make abstractions. In the teeming world of Funes, there were only details, almost immediate in their presence. Hurley's Collected Fictions reads To think is to ignore (or forget) differences, to generalize, to abstract, and Hurley does not even keep the title: he prints the story as Funes, His Memory, on the argument that memorioso is colloquial in Spanish and memorious is not. The three renderings are also separated cleanly by the enumeration sentence, and the scan I read gives the Kerrigan form of it, He told me that toward 1886 he had devised a new system of enumeration, against Irby's in 1886 he had invented an original system of numbering and Hurley's in 1886 he had invented a numbering system original with himself. So the note names the wrong translator for the wording it is ruling out, and it says the proposed wording is not in the Ficciones text as though that were a fault in the proposal, when the proposal never claimed Ficciones: it claimed Labyrinths, and on the evidence I can reach it claimed it correctly. The correction was made because Labyrinths could not be opened, not because anything was shown to be wrong. Two ways to close this. Preferred: keep the Kerrigan source line exactly as it stands, since it is the one wording I have confirmed from a scan with a translator credit attached, and replace the note with an honest one, for example that the line is quoted in Kerrigan's Ficciones rendering, verified in the Grove text, and that the more widely circulated wording, To think is to forget differences, generalize, make abstractions, is Irby's in Labyrinths and is a different translation of the same sentence. Alternative: restore the proposal as filed, Irby and Labyrinths, but only if a re-verifier can actually open a Labyrinths page rather than a search summary, which I could not. Either way the sentence naming Hurley must go: nothing in it is true.
